content.text: Track what I eat and how much, with calories, history and trends.

content.reply:
I'd love to build this properly, but I have to be straight with you: the tracker you're describing needs three things Alpha can't do yet — saving your records on this Mac, showing them in a screen of their own with history and trends, and estimating calories for foods it doesn't already know. Those are all on the way, and I'll build the full tracker the moment they land.

What I can give you today is the calculating half: you paste in a day's meals with portions, and it returns calories per item, per meal and for the day, measured against a target if you set one. It uses a built-in list of common foods and lets you add your own — but you'd re-paste each day, since nothing is stored yet.

Three quick things so I get it right.

interpretation.outcome: A food and calorie tracker with saved history and trends over time.
interpretation.main_input: What you ate and how much, entered day by day.
interpretation.useful_result: A running log you can look back on, plus daily totals and a trend showing whether you're above or below your usual intake.
important_assumptions: Calories in kcal, and days run midnight to midnight in your local time
Portions given in everyday units (1 cup, 2 eggs, 200 g) as well as grams
Right now the only piece Alpha can actually build is the calorie maths, run in the conversation — nothing is saved between messages
Foods Alpha doesn't recognise are flagged for you rather than guessed at

options: Built-in common foods, I'll fill gaps

content.reply:
Good — day-calculator it is, built on a list of common foods with you filling any gaps, and each day measured against a calorie target.

Here's how it'll work: you paste the day's meals with portions and your target (e.g. 'target 2000 — breakfast: 2 eggs, 1 slice toast; lunch: 200g chicken, 1 cup rice'), and you get back calories per item, a subtotal per meal, the day's total, and how far over or under you are. Anything not on the built-in list comes back flagged rather than guessed — tell me 'protein bar = 220' and it folds into the totals and sticks for the rest of that conversation.

Two limits worth repeating: nothing is saved yet, so you'll re-state your target and meals each new conversation, and there's no history or trend view until saved records and a screen of its own arrive. I'll build the full tracker on top of this the moment they do.

interpretation.outcome: A day-calculator you paste meals into: it returns calories per item, a subtotal per meal, the day's total, and how far over or under your daily calorie target you are.
interpretation.main_input: Free-form text you type in the conversation, e.g. 'breakfast: 2 eggs, 1 slice toast; lunch: 200g chicken, 1 cup rice' plus your target number.
interpretation.useful_result: A tidy breakdown in the reply: each food with its portion and calories, per-meal subtotals, a day total, an over/under line against your target, and a separate list of anything it doesn't recognise so nothing is silently guessed.
important_assumptions: Calories in kcal; portions accepted in grams, millilitres and household units (cup, slice, piece, tbsp) or plain item counts
Calories come from a built-in list of common foods; anything missing is flagged and you can supply the number, which is reused for the rest of that conversation
Meals grouped as breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks unless you label them otherwise
You state your calorie target alongside the day's meals (or once in a conversation), since nothing can be saved yet
Protein is left out for now — calories only
Results appear in the conversation; nothing is stored between conversations

briefs.success_summary: Alpha replies with a tidy breakdown: each food with its portion and calories, a subtotal per meal, a day total, and an over/under line against the target. Anything it can't recognise is listed separately so nothing is silently guessed.

content.text: Turn my meeting notes into a one-page brief I can send to my team.
Every morning, send my mom a WhatsApp message with today's weather for Ahmedabad.

content.reply:
I have to be straight with you about two things first. Alpha can't send WhatsApp messages — no messaging service is connected, and that isn't planned for the first release. It also can't look up the weather on its own (web access isn't connected yet), and it can't run anything automatically every morning (local schedules aren't connected yet either).

What I can build today is the piece in the middle: a little morning message writer. You glance at your weather app, give it the high, low, conditions and rain chance, and it hands you a finished message in your voice that you paste into your mom's WhatsApp chat. Ten seconds of your morning instead of composing it yourself.

Two things would shape it, then I'll make it.

interpretation.outcome: Your mom gets a short daily WhatsApp message with Ahmedabad's weather for the day.
interpretation.main_input: Today's Ahmedabad forecast (high, low, conditions, chance of rain), which you read off your weather app.
interpretation.useful_result: A ready-to-send message in your own voice that you paste into WhatsApp in a few seconds each morning — because Alpha cannot fetch the weather or send WhatsApp messages itself yet.
important_assumptions: Temperatures in °C, since this is for Ahmedabad.
One message per morning, addressed to your mom, warm and short (2–3 lines).
You supply the forecast figures; Alpha never invents or estimates them.
Nothing is stored between mornings — each message is composed fresh.

questions.question: What language and tone should the message be in?
options: Something else — send me a sample line you'd write
questions.why_it_matters: It changes every word of the output, and a message to your mom should sound like you.

questions.question: Besides the temperature, what should each message include?
options: Add a short care line (carry an umbrella, drink water, etc.)
questions.why_it_matters: It decides what the writer asks you for each morning and what counts as a complete message.

briefs.goal: Give Kenil a finished, warm morning WhatsApp message about Ahmedabad's weather that he can copy and send to his mom in seconds.
briefs.success_summary: Kenil supplies the day's forecast figures; within one exchange he gets a complete 2–3 line message in his chosen language that he pastes into WhatsApp without editing.

primary_journey.action: Kenil opens Alpha in the morning and gives today's Ahmedabad forecast: high, low, conditions, and chance of rain.
primary_journey.expected_result: The writer accepts the figures and confirms what it received.
A finished message in his chosen language and tone appears, mentioning Ahmedabad, the day's temperature range and conditions, plus a short care line where it fits.

primary_journey.action: Kenil copies the message and pastes it into his mom's WhatsApp chat.
primary_journey.expected_result: Message sent by Kenil himself; Alpha does not touch WhatsApp.

actions.title: Write today's weather message for mom
actions.description: Takes the day's Ahmedabad forecast figures supplied by Kenil and turns them into a short, warm WhatsApp message in the chosen language: a greeting, the temperature range and conditions, an optional care line tied to the weather (heat, rain, cold), and a warm sign-off. Pure wording work — it does not look up weather or guess missing figures.
inputs: conditions in plain words (sunny, cloudy, rain)
chance of rain as a percentage (optional)
outputs: finished message text ready to copy into WhatsApp

actions.title: Check the forecast details are complete
actions.description: Looks at what Kenil supplied and, if something needed is missing or impossible (no high temperature, a low above the high, a rain chance outside 0–100), says plainly what it needs instead of producing a half-written message.
outputs: either a green light, or a short note naming exactly what is missing or wrong

constraints: Alpha cannot send the message — Kenil pastes it into WhatsApp himself.
Alpha cannot fetch the forecast — every figure comes from Kenil.
Alpha cannot run this automatically each morning — Kenil starts it.
Never invent or estimate a temperature that was not supplied.
Message stays under about 300 characters so it reads well in a chat.

acceptance_examples.description: A normal warm Ahmedabad day, English tone, with a care line.

expected.message: Good morning Mummy! Ahmedabad today: partly cloudy, 27–34°C, with a small 20% chance of rain. Keep water with you if you go out in the afternoon. Love you ❤️

acceptance_examples.description: Heavy rain day — the care line must match the weather rather than be generic.

expected.message: Good morning Mummy! Ahmedabad today: heavy rain, 25–29°C, 95% chance of rain through the day. Please carry an umbrella and avoid the low-lying roads. Love you ❤️
expected.note: Care line refers to rain and roads, not to heat or drinking water.

acceptance_examples.description: Kenil gives conditions but forgets the temperatures.

expected.response: I need today's high and low for Ahmedabad before I can write it — what are they?

acceptance_examples.description: The low is higher than the high, so one figure is wrong.

expected.response: The low (31°C) is above the high (24°C) — could you check which is which?

assumptions.text: Celsius, with Ahmedabad as the fixed city.
Message is addressed to your mom and ends with a warm sign-off; hand me a sample and I'll match your phrasing.
The finished message appears right here in the conversation, ready to copy.
No history of past messages is kept, since record storage isn't connected yet.

options: Add a short care line (carry an umbrella, drink water, etc.)

http — web and API access is not connected yet, so Alpha cannot look up the Ahmedabad forecast; you supply the figures
schedules — local schedules are not connected yet, so this cannot run by itself every morning
